item.title: Strip Clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6, and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs.
item.description:
Strip clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6, and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs.
"I’m fascinated with the attention to detail from Rockstar," said the head choreographer, Brooke Wilde. "I spent hours in Jack of Hearts and Delights Cabaret, mastering each performance to bring back to Spearmint, and now obsessed gamers can put down their controllers, get out of the bedroom, and experience their favourite virtual lap dances with the Spearmint Rhino girls in the real world. While the in-game strip clubs are addictive, nothing beats the real thing.”
While we can't be sure exactly how many people are reaching out to their local strip joints for IRL GTA-inspired bodily contact, you have to respect the hustle. It's also an interesting counterpoint given GTA 6's impact on another part of the adult entertainment industry, with Mashable reporting that Pornhub saw a 15.5% drop an hour after the game was released on November 19.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
Spearmint Rhino's relationship with the series actually goes back to 2013 and GTA 5, when Rockstar used a play on the name of the clubs, Vanilla Rhino, and Rockstar has said that developers for GTA 6 visited strip clubs in Miami and Florida (where Spearmint Rhino has one of its venues) for research purposes.
In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia can both go to strip clubs either together as a couple or individually, and can opt-in for VIP lap dances. As explained in our GTA 6 sex and romance guide, you can throw money at dancers, and if you throw most of your money at one dancer they will remove some of their clothes.
“While gamers across the world immerse themselves in virtual worlds, demand for authentic real-world experiences has never been higher and we’ve had hundreds of inquiries from GTA 6 fans," explained the company president and COO, Kathy Vercher.
"Strip clubs are such an iconic feature in the franchise, and Spearmint Rhino is uniquely positioned to create a real-world experience for gamers. Thanks to the dedication of our Chief Choreographer, Brooke, we’ve been able to bring the in-game lap dance experience into our venues worldwide, with such accuracy that gamers are guaranteed to get a mindblowing real-life experience.”

item.title: Abby actor Laura Bailey reflects on how pre-release leaks and online misinformation made The Last of Us Part 2's backlash so much worse.
item.description:
The Last of Us Part 2 actress Laura Bailey has reflected on how the game's pre-release leaks and the subsequent spread of misinformation made its ensuing online backlash much worse.
More than six years after The Last of Us Part 2 leaks ignited controversy online and sparked a wave of death threats towards Bailey and her family, the prolific video game voice actress has now labelled Naughty Dog's highly-anticipated sequel as being "cursed" from the off.
While acknowledging that the game's bold narrative choices would always have been polarizing, Bailey blamed the level of vitriol directed specifically at her on the leaks of specific scenes involving her character Abby that spoiled major plot points — and did so without the game's intended narrative context. Because of this, she believes, online outrage had already hardened across social media long before launch day.
Warning! If you're still worried about The Last of Us Part 2 spoilers, now's a good time to head elsewhere.
The Last of Us Day 2026 Announcements
"That game got cursed by so many different elements," Bailey said, appearing on the Mythical Kitchen podcast. "It got leaked, nobody knew the full story and all that got leaked were these horrific scenes. It had been leaked that there's a trans character in the game. The scene comes out where [Abby] has got a golf club. It just turned into a nightmare online.
"They were looking into all of the active death threats that were coming in," Bailey continued. "Because it was constant. They threatening my parents, they were threatening my baby."
The leak of various cutscenes in April 2020 — several months before The Last of Us Part 2's official release — led franchise steward Neil Druckmann to say he had been left "heartbroken" at their impact after working for years on the game. Naughty Dog issued an official statement pleading with fans not to spread the spoilers further online but, predictably, such was the fan investment in The Last of Us Part 1's duo of Ellie and Joel that word of the latter's abrupt murder by Abby spread quickly across the internet.
"I knew it was going to get a reaction because Joel is beloved and he is an amazing character," Bailey noted. "I loved him. I knew that was coming. But because of the leaks, it was just a lot. Up until then I was very present online and I shared a lot of my sense online. I kind of backed off after that.
"The haters are very loud online," she concluded, "but there's a ton of people that love that game and still come up at cons to me, and are dressed as Abbie and say she changed their life and it's an amazing game. And it is, it's beautiful and the message of it is beautiful."
Despite all of that, Bailey went on to win Best Performance at The Game Awards 2020, while IGN's The Last of Us: Part 2 returned a perfect 10/10 score.
Photo by Rodin Eckenroth/WireImage.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
item.description:
Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
Yesterday, in an interview with CNBC, President Trump told reporters that he convinced Nvidia's board to take Huang back, saying he "made the deal" and that he "gave them assurances, at least everything we knew" that the CEO's return wasn't a risk to national security.
Trump also took to social media to celebrate after the announcement, even posting a meme with Jensen Huang in Donald Trump's place after the assassination attempt in Pennsylvania, but instead of raising a fist in defiance, Huang is holding up a red bra.
While Trump seems happy that Huang has returned, the reinstated CEO now has to face both houses of Congress in hearings about Nvidia's compliance with export controls. Politicians from both parties are demanding answers about how many GPUs have been exported to embargoed countries like China and Russia.
Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted on X / Twitter: "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and Nvidia still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement."
What's more surprising is that Senator John Curtis, a Republican from Utah, echoed Warren's concerns, posting on X / Twitter: "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"
Despite these ongoing concerns, at least some Nvidia employees seem happy with Huang's return. An Nvidia employee posted a video on X / Twitter, below, of Huang getting a standing ovation in the lobby of the company's headquarters.
if you come for the king, you best not miss https://t.co/yb2eV1d5do
It's unsurprising that Huang would be welcomed back in this way, after an internal movement among employees to reinstate the CEO picked up quite a bit of steam immediately after his resignation. But while there was a crowd of cheering employees, there are at least some employees who feel like his return is a mistake, with one engineer anonymously telling Yahoo Finance: "This is the worst outcome. We already paid the price of his departure but are still saddled with working for a jerk."
In the fallout of Huang's departure, reports emerged that painted a picture of his management style. For example, he allegedly told one employee that he'd "pee on [their] brain."
It's still early days for Huang's return to Nvidia, and with everything that's happened in the last two weeks, it's impossible to guess what's going to happen next. But now that his return has breathed new life into the AI market, it's unlikely that RAM prices are going to come down any time soon.
Photographer: Ken Cedeno/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images.

item.title: Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover. Check out this first look.
item.description:
Scott Pilgrim takes on the world of Fortnite later this week, with the battle royale's next crossover.
Character skins for Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers will become available via the Shop for an as-yet undisclosed amount of V-Bucks. To be clear, these are the graphic novel versions of the characters — so no Michael Cera in Fortnite, yet.
Epic Games announced the collaboration today via a teaser trailer showing off both character skins in action (Ramona has multiple hair style options, I can see), riffing on the story's plot of Scott defeating a league of evil ex-partners.
Other Fortnite shenanigans we've learned of today: a Puss in Boots collaboration is next on the docket (and yes, Puss will be a pet-like Sidekick) before the current mini-season is done. Speaking of which, Fortnite's big year-end live event is currently slated for December 5, which is also when the game will hold its next Community Day.
Hop into Fortnite then for a smattering of free cosmetics, watch on Twitch for a free golden Jonesy skin, and if you've picked up at least 800 V-Bucks at some point this season you'll get the long-teased pirate Hope skin. Exactly what's set to happen during the event remains to be seen, but the stage is set for Fortnite's uber big bad Geno to finally get his come-uppance (again), while the mysterious Captain X will reveal his true identity after recently crashing a real-life awards show. Here's hoping it's not Mr. Beast.
How's Fortnite doing right now? The launch of GTA 6 has naturally had some impact on its daily active player count, though Alinea Analytics noted the battle royale had recovered well following Rockstar's big launch last week. The same cannot be said for Call of Duty, with active HQ users down 40% since GTA 6's launch. It seems fair to suggest that COD's audience is more aligned with GTA's, but Fortnite has also reaped the rewards of its current mini-season allowing players to win a fortnight of free access to the game's Shop — something many players have been grinding for, despite low odds.
What's next for Fortnite? While Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney spends his time on X / Twitter discussing AI and various other subjects, his team will launch the game's Chapter 8 incarnation following that December 8 in-game event. As of yet, nothing major has leaked for what's in store.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
item.description:
We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
Instead of playing the game as intended and robbing stores, banks, and gang hideouts, some GTA 6 players are repeating the same actions over and over to generate money fast.
How to do the new GTA 6 money glitch
The new method sees players using vans and character swaps at a location in a town called Hamlet. In Hamlet, there’s an industrial area with a big warehouse outside of town, with a teddy bear van parked outside.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
There are drugs inside the van outside as well as inside the warehouse itself. To do the glitch, you need to register two vans, turn up to the location, and have your partner call in a different personal vehicle while the player calls in one of the personal vans and takes the loot.
Stow the loot in the back of your personal vehicle, then drive the teddy van parked outside into the warehouse, parking it inside, on the right of the door, at which point tell your partner to wait in the car. The player then gets out and drives the teddy bear van parked inside (both of these vans are empty of loot at this point) and park this opposite the other van, so both vans have their back doors facing the shutter entrance.
Next, switch to your partner and exit the first teddy van before heading outside, where you switch back. Then ask your partner to drive the personal van loaded with all the loot. Using the partner menu, ask your partner to fence the loot, and watch them drive off to do so.
Once your partner has driven off, use the Scooter Bros app to call in the second personal van. After backing the van up to the warehouse, switch to the partner fencing the loot, before immediately switching back. This respawns both teddy bear vans and the loot inside, but it also keeps the two you moved earlier where you parked them inside and fills them with loot, essentially doubling the take.
According to one GTA 6 player who posted about this new method on Reddit, the technique earns you between $88,000-$100,000 in under 10 minutes.
Some of the replies to the Reddit post asked the OP when their in-game bank account limit will be raised, suggesting they’re still relatively early in the game. Later on, more lucrative robbery opportunities open up for players anyway, and you can pull off $100k jobs with way less hassle than this, and while having some actual fun whilst you’re at it.
The question is whether Rockstar patches early days money glitches like these out of GTA 6. GTA 6's first post-launch patch failed to take action, but I imagine it won't be long before Rockstar does something about this.

item.title: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
item.description:
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
Dawn of War 4, developed by King Art Games, launches with four playable races: the Space Marines; Orks, Necrons, and the Adeptus Mechanicus. We knew that the developer had plans to release more factions over time, as has been the case with previous entries in the real-time strategy series. But we didn’t know which would come first… until now.
Warning! Potential spoilers for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 follow.
The teaser ends with a tease for Dawn of War 4’s first DLC faction. We see the unmistakable eyes of Vashtorr the Arkifane, alongside the narration: “And what began on Aurelia is coming to Kronus.”
That’s a clear reference to Chaos as the new faction, given Aurelia, the former homeworld and capital of the Blood Ravens Space Marine Chapter, was gobbled up by the Warp (Warhammer 40,000’s version of a hell dimension full of demons), before it was spat out and besieged by Black Legion Chaos Space Marines. So, it would make sense that Chaos Space Marines are the new faction. Will we see further corruption of the Blood Ravens play out?
Who is Vashtorr the Arkifane?
But what about Vashtorr the Arkifane? Vashtorr is a sort of in-between, Chaos Undivided being who appears to have designs on becoming the fifth Chaos god. According to the lore, Vashtorr came into existence within the Warp due to our obsessive pursuit of tech innovation (feels pretty relatable right now, doesn’t it?). As such, Vashtorr acts as a sort of arms dealer to the existing Chaos factions, creating powerful daemon weapons and engines for use in war.
Ever since Vashtorr’s dramatic introduction into the Warhammer 40,000 universe with the Arks of Omen storyline a few years ago, and his uneasy alliance with Horus’ successor, Abaddon the Despoiler, fans have wondered about his masterplan. As is Games Workshop’s want, the overarching Warhammer 40,000 storyline moves slowly, so we don’t really have much to go on beyond he’s big, he’s mean, and he wants it all. Perhaps Dawn of War 4 will shed more light on his motivations?
Either way, it would be really cool if we got to actually command Vashtorr on the battlefield, although you’d expect him to be incredibly overpowered, given what we know of his power set from the lore. Dawn of War 4 is the first Warhammer 40,000 video game to feature a playable Primarch (one of the Emperor’s ultra powerful sons). Could we see Lion El'Jonson go up against Vashtorr in the DLC? That would be quite something.
It’s not long before we find out. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.

item.title: Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
item.description:
Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
With the massive crossover movie set to hit theaters next month, Stan was recently asked about Bucky's long-term future in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — and his response did little to calm nervous fans.
Having debuted all the way back in 2011's Captain America: The First Avenger, Bucky is one of the last remaining Phase One veterans still standing on the front lines. Now, with his old pal Steve Rogers back front and center for this next installment, many fans have long suspected Bucky's 15-year arc could be about to culminate with a long-awaited reunion followed by a tragic end.
Avengers: Doomsday Poster Montage Gallery
"I'm always happy to keep playing him," Stan said, while appearing recently on the Next Best Picture podcast. "I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately.
"I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways," he continued, "but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far."
To be fair to Stan, after appearances in nine films and his own Disney+ spinoff, it's hard to know exactly where the character can continue to evolve. He is arguably the most experienced member of the New Avengers team, but this is a role that could also be provided by Yelena Belova. He has long since redeemed himself for his days as the Winter Soldier. And with Steve's story (presumably) wrapped up again with these latest Avengers movies, it's unclear what else there is for Bucky to do.
Stan has attempted to pitch a Bucky solo project to Marvel in the past — a thriller movie in the same vein as Denis Villeneuve-directed thriller Sicario — but noted again here that he had only received a non-commital response from MCU boss Kevin Feige.
"I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," Stan concluded. "I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those."
While Bucky is beloved by MCU fans, Doomsday's apparent focus on the returning Steve Rogers provides a potentially unique narrative oppurtunity for the two characters' time-travelling bromance to reach an emotional conclusion. Will Bucky repay Steve for saving him by sacrificing his own life? Or will Doom simply kill him to upset Steve? Regardless of what happens, it's worth recalling something Chris Evans said recently of his character's own "brutal" arc in Doomsday:
"The Russos love beating up Steve Rogers," Evans remarked. "Their favourite thing to do is to just beat the crap out of him. To them that's what makes a hero, and that's someone who gets punched so many times but still gets up. So they keep finding new ways to kick his butt but this one was brutal, and a really good examination into his nature and his values."
What better way to knock Steve down than for Doom to kill Cap's original wingman? (And perhaps we should also be worried for Steve's son too, especially as the suggestion is that Doom is seeking revenge for the loss of his own loved ones.)
Of course, nothing yet is certain — and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars is expected to provide something of another MCU reset, meaning any death in Doomsday may not necessarily prove permanent. Still, thinking back to Avengers: Endgame, a few of its biggest deaths have been left as-is so as to not undermine their impact — something a tragic fate for Bucky would likely also qualify for.
The fate of the multiverse — and one James Buchanan "Bucky" Barnes — will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18.
Image credit: Marvel.

item.title: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates.
item.description:
BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates, one of the game's writers has said.
For more than a decade, Mass Effect fans have debated how BioWare could reconcile the wildly divergent endings of Mass Effect 3 — and satisfy players who insisted that their particular ending choice should be canon (I see you, Destroy fans). But according to one of the writers behind the now-canceled Mass Effect Universe, the studio had actually cracked the puzzle before EA scrapped the project and closed BioWare forever.
Speaking during a reddit fan Q&A supporting the "Save Mass Effect" fan movement, Mass Effect: Annihilation novel author Cat Valente — who spent three years on the writing team for the unfinished sequel — offered a bittersweet glimpse into how the narrative team approached the franchise's biggest lingering questions.
While strict NDAs signed with published EA continue to prevent Valente from revealing specific plot details, she emphasized that reconciling Mass Effect 3's endings was front and center for the game's writers room, and noted that the team wasn't relying on a single silver bullet to bridge the 600-year narrative gap between the original trilogy and this upcoming fifth installment.
Every IGN Mass Effect Review
"[We] worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel," Valente wrote.
"Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall f***ing order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard.* An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible... it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.
"And it's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it's easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a *video game*?
"But we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she concluded. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that."
As a hugely knowledgeable fan of the original trilogy — enough that she got the gig writing Andromeda's quarian ark prequel novel — Valente emphasized that the fates of the trilogy's loyal squadmates had also been a key consideration for the Mass Effect Universe team.
"You would have been able to know everything you wanted to know about them," she said, when asked for her own thoughts of what characters such as Garrus, Tali and Wrex did next. "I don't have headcanons about those fates, I have canon-canons. I know you'd have been able to find out about them because one of my jobs was to write all those fates and their possible variations (all then submitted to the room, workshopped with everyone, and sent to higher-ups for approval...)
"God, it was like being asked to stitch a nice border on the Shroud of Turin," she continued. "I put on my Big Writer Pants for that one and gave it every bit of talent I have, because I love those characters beyond measure, and they more than earned my best."
Of course, we know that Universe would have seen at least one fan-favorite character return: Liara, now 600 years older — around middle age for a long-lived asari. But what about others? Asked for specifics, Valente noted her NDA blocked her from confirming specific names, but that there had been widespread discussion of bringing back every character possible.
"I think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically *could* survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them," Valente teased. "We thought about all the things you'd have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it's the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously."
Which Mass Effect Story Do You Want the Show to Follow?

item.title: GTA 6 actor Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online.
item.description:
GTA 6 actor Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online.
Warning! Spoilers for Mandy's role in GTA 6 follow.
Lexie Shoaibi did performance capture and voice over for Mandy, a woman you meet early on in the game. Mandy asks Jason to fix a clogged sink in her house, but comes out in a tiny bikini once he’s under the sink with a wrench. It didn't take long for the internet to latch on to Mandy, with countless social media posts discussing the character.
Shoaibi appeared on a Hasan Piker stream a few days ago, chatting about GTA 6 while raising money for charity. During the stream, she spoke about the newfound fame and reaction to her character.
“I don’t know how that happened,” Shoaibi said. “People pretending to be me? It’s thrilling. Please stop, but it’s also so exciting. It’s sort of bittersweet.”
Shoaibi hinted at this issue in a seperate Instagram post in which she warned her followers about fake accounts from people trying to impersonate her on social media. Referring to one X / Twitter account that has popped up in the last week purporting to be her own, she said: "This is fake! I don’t have a Twitter! This isn’t me! Please, someone, make it go away, ew!”
Meanwhile, Shoaibi revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar.
Warning! Specific Mandy spoilers follow.
Despite Mandy only being a minor character in Chapter 1, Rockstar’s attention to detail put a bit of a spotlight on the character. As well as her basically being nude, the garden outside Mandy’s house hides a dark secret. When Jason is fixing the sink, he finds something clogged in it. You might think it’s a chicken bone, but closer inspection shows it’s a severed human finger. Check the trunk of Mandy’s car and you can find a kill kit. Have a nosey around her back garden and you’ll find vats of acid and a freshly dug grave. The game basically hints that she’s not a harmless stalker — she’s a serial killer. No, you can’t “fix her.”
“She’s a lot of fun, so if you play the game, let me know if you find me,” Shoaibi said in another statement about her character before people made it weird. “Y’all there aren’t words!!!! Thank you so much for the love and support. This is crazy!! Ily forever!”

item.title: Why GTA 6 user reviews are so low: Metacritic review-bombing explained.
item.description:
GTA 6 tied with the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-scored game in history based on Metacritic ratings, sitting pretty at a 99 critic score. Rarely do we see something earn this kind of unanimous praise, but our reviewer Luke Reilly would agree, giving GTA 6 a coveted score of 10 on our scale and calling it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played." However, you may have heard about the wide discrepancy between the critic's metascore and the user score — as of publishing this, GTA 6 has a 5.7/10 average from well over 100,000 user reviews. Why is that?
User scores on Metacritic are under far, far (and I mean far) less scrutiny, allowing everyone and anyone to post their own review and score regardless of how much of the game they've actually played. This isn't anything new, and it’s been around on other sites that aggregate scores from the audience (like Rotten Tomatoes or an older version of GameSpot I used to use as a kid). As a result, you're likely to see more outliers or trolling, but mostly users who shoot from the hip to let their voice be heard. That leaves things susceptible to review bombing – typically, a wave of reactionary people who have motives beyond evaluating a game for what it is.
There are reviews that appear to have legitimate concerns, mentioning that GTA 6 might not be for them or align with their tastes. Among those concerns are a slow start that emphasizes slice-of-life style activities before action starts to pick up, dissatisfaction with the interactive layers for simple tasks, the frame rate being capped at 30fps, or a general disinterest in what it's trying to do as an open-world action game. Maybe it didn't live up to their perceived "hype" with 13 years between series entries. However, you might be wondering why GTA 6 is the latest subject of what's clearly motivated review bombing with tons of "0" scores from a reactionary crowd.
GTA 6 Bikini Girl Screenshots
I'm not going to pretend to give credence to clearly disingenuous reviews, but if you are genuinely curious, there are a significant number of reviews that decry GTA 6 for being "too woke" and a, uh, "cuck simulator” — the most unserious people, the incel crowd coming out of the woodwork, trying to fight a weird culture war over a game they likely either did not play or have barely played. GTA has always parodied the most ridiculous parts of American culture, and GTA 6 is no exception — now the primary targets of that satire are crying about it.
I don't think I need to explain what it means to be a "cuck" or the concept of cuckoldry, but by definition, it has nothing to do with anything that happens to you or that you have to do in GTA 6. And perhaps the most telling part of it all is the complaints of "woke" (another term that has been ground to a point of no meaning, co-opted by right-wing extremists to label anything they deem politically progressive).
In large part, GTA 6 is telling a love story where two partners, the protagonists Jason and Lucia, have a believable relationship on-screen with corresponding gameplay elements in addition to their Bonnie and Clyde-esque crime sprees. Maybe you don't want to put up drywall, renovate your house, or run errands in early missions, but what you're about to read is more telling about the kind of people review-bombing the game than the content of the game itself.
Sift through the negative reviews on Metacritic and it's a trove of entries that read, "Everything that represents the woke culture don’t deserve nothing, other than zero." Or, "GTA 6 is way too woke for my taste." And other variations on one that reads, "Graphics fantastic, besides that a cuckhold [sic] game, and really woke!" One just spams the word "woke" while several are straight gibberish or admittance that they did not play the game.
One entry reads, "I already have an annoying gf in real life and you want me to deal with it in the game again???????", while another says, "No hookers, no freedom, No action, Just cuck simulator, Please woke community, leave Rockstar games alone." And (sorry) one more for the road: "The plot is boring, and the main characters are a simp and a stereotypical ‘strong woman.’ They have absolutely no charisma; the game is packed with a one-sided agenda, and the trolling of ‘libturds’ is dull and predictable."
Amid this all, Metacritic has some measures in place to moderate fake reviews — it removed user reviews that went live before the game even released. And its 36-hour rule has been in place for a while where user reviews can't go up until a day-and-a-half has passed from a game's public release. Moderators also have the ability to stamp out reviews that violate Metacritic's guidelines, but with well over 100,000 of them up now, it's a gargantuan task.

item.title: GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
item.description:
GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
If you're an Expansion Pack subscriber, you can now update your Nintendo Classics GameCube app to gain access to the cult classic aquatic racer — and also unlock the ability to remove the app's annoying border graphics.
The Nintendo Classic apps have a border gradient that until now you couldn't remove — and it's something that's proven a bugbear from fans who want a cleaner look. For now, only the GameCube app has the option to simply have clear black borders instead, though it seems likely the other console apps will follow. Or, maybe this is something only the technical power of Switch 2 can pull off?
"Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves!" reads an official blurb for the game. "Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms... Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!"
Wave Race: Blue Storm becomes the 12th GameCube title available on Switch 2 via the Expansion Pack subscription service, following the previous additions of Chibi-Robo!, F-Zero GX, Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, Luigi's Mansion, Super Mario Strikers, Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, SoulCalibur 2, Star Fox Adventures, Super Mario Sunshine, The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker and Wario World.

item.title: Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
item.description:
Now that the dust has somewhat settled after the avalanche that was the launch of GTA 6, PlayStation has revealed some of its stats from the game, revealing that this was the single largest game release in PlayStation history.
PlayStation’s November 23 blog post states that more than 39 million unique players have played the game on the PlayStation 5, setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any PlayStation game. This beats out other records for multiplayer games, single-player games, and perhaps most astonishingly, even free-to-play titles.
On top of that, GTA 6 players logged a total of 683 million hours played in the game, with the average player spending an estimated 17.4 hours sticking up virtual pawn shops and stealing NPC’s cars during its first few days.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
What’s more impressive is the sheer amount of people who purchased PS5s specifically to play GTA 6. PlayStation’s blog says it saw the “largest number of newly-connected PS5 consoles on a single day” since the console’s launch in November 2020, not counting end-of-year holidays like Christmas. Since GTA 6’s launch, it was the first game played on 70% of these new consoles.
GTA 6 has, perhaps unsurprisingly, broken a slew of big records. The most prominent of these is its status as the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with Rockstar reporting that the game earned $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours.
On top of this, internet provider Comcast said that GTA 6’s launch day was its highest-traffic day ever, with 24% of all its internet traffic during peak times coming from users downloading and playing Rockstar’s latest offering. Xbox had its own big records, too; Xfinity, which is under the Comcast umbrella, said GTA 6 increased the internet traffic on Xbox consoles by four times the normal amount this November.
People are still making new discoveries in this game, and there’s bound to be many more that pop up over the next few months. GTA 6 is up for eight awards at The Game Awards and has enjoyed massive critical reception, with IGN scoring it a glowing 10 out of 10 — the title of ‘Masterpiece.’ Reviewer Luke Reilly praised the game for being “exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered,” saying “Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played.”
It’s unlikely that we see a game release as big as this one, with such a massive cultural impact, ever again. Rockstar certainly set a new standard for the industry with this one, to the point where many users aren’t sure if a photo they see online is from the real world or from the game.

item.title: A new report claims that Call of Duty saw an over 40% drop in players following GTA 6's release.
item.description:
A new report claims that Call of Duty saw an over 40% drop in players following GTA 6's release.
We've known all year long that Rockstar Games was going to dominate the final two months of 2026 thanks to the release of GTA 6. It's why a lot of publishers moved their games either into 2027 or pushed them up to September to steer clear of the blast radius. Call of Duty, however, releases on an annual cycle around October or November, which means Modern Warfare 4's post-launch plans were beginning right around the time of GTA 6's launch.
According to Alinea Analytics, it appears that Call of Duty lost almost half of its player base during GTA 6's record-breaking launch weekend. The Call of Duty app (which consists of Warzone, Black Ops 7, and Modern Warfare 4) saw a 42% drop across platforms, taking the overall daily player count from 7.6 million users to 4.4 million users. There's likely a lot of crossover between GTA and Call of Duty's audiences, so it's no surprise to see a drop in players, but nearly half clearly highlights just how much of an event GTA 6 is.
Call of Duty app (MW4, Warzone, and BO7) lost 42% of players following GTA 6's launch, down from 7.6M daily active users to 4.4M PS5 saw the biggest drop off out of all platforms with 44% decline in players, per Alinea Analytics https://t.co/cARXye3Ahs
Earlier this fall, Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl stated that he believed GTA 6 would actually help Call of Duty, as the open-world crime epic would drive more attention toward gaming as a whole. People are buying new consoles or dusting off old ones to play this game, so in theory, they will turn their attention toward other titles once they are done with GTA. Whether that title is Call of Duty remains to be seen, but currently, it appears to only be hurting the series in the immediate short term. Things will probably bounce back up, but it'll be interesting to see how many people return.
This also may not be the last time Call of Duty takes a hit from GTA 6. There are expected to be at least two more big beats or launches for this game, with the PC release rumored for an early 2027 release. However, the even bigger moment will come in the form in the inevitable online mode. Rockstar hasn't talked about its plans for GTA 6's online offerings yet, but it's highly speculated to release sometime next year. If it drops in the summer, it may not hurt Call of Duty a ton since that is the period where the most hardcore fans are still grinding away on the game.
But if GTA 6 Online dropped next fall, around October or November, it could put Call of Duty in a really difficult position. It'll be an interesting story to follow, but Call of Duty has been battling intense competition for two straight years now thanks to Battlefield 6 in 2025 and GTA 6 this year. Maybe it can contend next year, but the jury is still out.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027.
item.description:
Ted Lasso is coming back to Apple TV for a fifth season, with production set to begin in April 2027.
Apple TV’s beloved comedy series is coming back for another season, and it’s possible that there’s more in store. As pointed out by Variety, Jackson Sudeikis — who will return as both executive producer and star of the show — said he “would like to” continue the project through a sixth season in an October episode of Talk Easy with Sam Fragoso.
“Yeah, I just don’t know,” he told the host when asked about the topic, clarifying that he wasn’t holding anything back “intentionally.” “We haven’t started a writers’ room or anything like that,” he added.
Ted Lasso: Season 2 Photos
For now, we know that Season 5 is in the bag, but this isn’t a huge surprise. In fact, it was almost a given, seeing how Season 4 was Apple TV’s biggest launch in the platform’s history. Its premiere garnered an astonishing 296.6 million minutes watched, proving the audience’s interest even after its initial storyline wrapped up at the end of Season 3.
Now, Ted’s on a new mission: to coach a women’s football team. The newly formed second-division team, the Lady Greyhounds, take Ted on a parallel journey with new obstacles, primarily navigating the environment of women’s athletics and the unique challenges that come with it.
Ted Lasso has been a hugely successful show, both among fans and critics alike. We at IGN scored its first season a glowing 9 out of 10, calling it a “relentlessly optimistic and disarmingly charming comedy” that was sorely needed when it was released back in 2020. And while our review of the Season 4 premiere was comparatively softer, it certainly resonated with audiences enough to warrant a continuation of its new storyline.
For those who are unfamiliar with the show, it follows the kind, optimistic Ted Lasso, an American college football coach who gets hired to help a struggling English football league whose owner secretly hopes it fails. It’s a delightful watch, and a premise that has continued to prove sorely sought-after in the six years since its initial release.
Ted Lasso streams exclusively on Apple TV. For more shows streaming on the service, you can check out every series that’s making its way to the platform this November, which includes movies and shows like 12 12 12, Way of the Warrior Kid, and Stick Season 2.

If you've ever seen a Wile E. Coyote cartoon, you probably know where this is going. The idea is that the painting on the wall looks so lifelike that anyone not hyper-focused on the details thinks they can drive straight through it like any other tunnel. item.title: The graphics in GTA 6 are so realistic that actual photos and videos are being mistaken as screenshots or clips from the game.
item.description:
The graphics in GTA 6 are so realistic that actual photos and videos are being mistaken as screenshots or clips from the game.
It feels like every social media platform is chock-full of posts about Rockstar’s latest release, which has cemented itself as the biggest entertainment launch of all time. Everybody’s talking about it; it’s practically impossible to scroll through your timeline without seeing it in some form or another.
GTA 6 is a good-looking game, to say the least, with some of the most realistic visuals we’ve seen in a digital world thus far — to the point where it’s genuinely hard to tell the difference between what’s from the game and what’s from real life.
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
For instance, a video taken from influencer India Love’s live stream sparked a swath of comments from viewers who had to do a double-take to make sure they weren’t watching a clip from GTA 6, partly owing to the lighting. If anything, that just goes to show how realistic the game’s lighting really is, with one user writing on Twitter/X, “Why is everything lit so well in that game? How did they do that?”
gta6 has pan seared my brain
“I was confused by your post because I didn't know what part of the game this is,” another commented, while another admitted that they “haven’t even played GTA 6 and I thought it was a clip from it at first.”
Another person posted photos of a shirtless Jack Donoghue posing in a speedboat at sea, prompting no end of comments mistaking him for someone’s Jason in the game.
“Close enough, welcome back Jason Duval,” one joked, while another remarked, “Why did I think that this was Jason from GTA for a second?”
@Charismah411 Why did I think that this was Jason from gta for a second
Someone else posted photos of their dog that they took on 35mm film, showing the fluffy pup playing on a basketball court — and once again, players couldn’t help but admit that they’d accidentally mistaken the pictures for GTA 6 screenshots.
“Everything is a GTA 6 screenshot now. I'm cooked,” one user said.
“Lowkey thought this was GTA 6, my brain is done,” another added.
Everything is a GTA 6 screenshot now. I'm cooked.
However, it’s likely that this trend isn’t solely due to GTA 6’s fantastic graphics; if you’re totally absorbed in something over a long enough period of time, you’re more likely to see patterns from that thing in other areas of your life. In other words, yes, GTA 6’s graphics are out of this world — but also, it’s impossible to get away from this game right now, and if you’re playing it, you’ve probably got ‘GTA 6 brain.’

item.title: GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a life and the system that breeds crime.
item.description:
GTA 6 is receiving praise for its commentary on how hard it is for felons to start a new life and the system that breeds crime.
In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia choose a life of crime in hopes of creating financial stability in their lives. Their goal isn't necessarily to get rich and buy flashy cars or a mansion, but so they can lay the foundation for their family. Although Jason runs drugs for a local crime boss, Lucia in particular is the one who really pushes them to take on more ambitious jobs. Some players felt that her decision-making at the start of the game was a bit reckless, given that she just got out of prison — but if you read her text messages, things begin to make a lot more sense.
Players realized that her parole officer had denied her petition to take a job at a local bar, one of her only options for employment because she knew someone who worked there that could vouch for her. Without that, her record as a convicted felon would make it difficult for employers to consider her for a position. Her PO also noted that she's overdue on paying court-ordered parole fees, which she can't pay because she doesn't have a job, putting her in a vicious cycle.
Lucia's willingness to get back into crime makes a lot more sense when you look at her texts with her PO and see that they denied her request to get a job but still wanted her to pay bills she has no money for https://t.co/HBfpsZEmz2
This pushes Lucia to get involved with shady characters who turn her life with Jason upside down. A number of fans have praised this particular narrative beat, including some who have worked within this very system.
"As someone who worked as part of the system years ago, not as a PO but a case manager, this is wildly accurate to real life," said X user Mgs2master. "Rockstar did their homework here."
"GTA 6 is brave enough to try and educate the player on how desperation can drive you to crime through how it incorporates gameplay mechanics into the story," said one player. "It's genuinely one of the best uses of ludonarrative I’ve ever seen, period. I am floored."
GTA 6: Photo Mode Gallery
"As someone who's had family that has had to go through this s**t, it's genuinely not satirical," said another user. "This is straight up just what happens. The system is designed to funnel criminals back into crime by denying them opportunities needed to rehabilitate themselves to keep prisons full."
Another person noted that this system blocks people out of having a reasonable chance of developing a good life: "The US has a recidivism problem because once you have a felony you're essentially locked out of a good chunk of employment and housing stuff, and then these orgs act surprised when people go back to crime. The econ equivalent of kicking people while they're down."
Rockstar Games writer Rupert Humphries told Love Magazine earlier this year that the "American Dream" as we know it has scaled down for many people with each passing GTA game. Now, people just want a foundation to live and build a family, but the state of the world has made that increasingly unattainable, and in the case of GTA 6, it leads to the characters taking matters into their own hands.
Jason and Lucia Screenshots
"Some would say the American Dream collapsed a long time ago," said Humphries. "With GTA 4, we told an immigrant’s story that was supposed to be a kind of hollow commentary on the illusion of America as a land of opportunity, and then we sort of doubled down on that with the cynicism of GTA 5. Maybe the American Dream is more modest now. It’s a house for your family and your loans paid off instead of wild success — but maybe today, that is just as out of reach for the average person. Miami and Southern Florida are a particular front line for this battle between astronomical wealth and unbounded ambition, creating a pressure cooker for all kinds of insanity."
Of course, GTA 6 is still fiction and isn't an endorsement of real crime, despite how much some people would like you to believe otherwise. It's more so putting two charcaters in these circumstances and seeing how they react to the cards they're dealt. There also wouldn't be much of a game if Lucia decided to just spend the rest of her days scrounging for minimum wage work, after all.
GTA 6 has been a roaring success so far, generating over $3.79 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours with over 32.5 million copies sold in pre-sales alone. The game is also a critical smash hit, tying with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the best reviewed video game in history on Metacritic. IGN gave GTA 6 a 10 out of 10, praising it for its depth and detail.
"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from the review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

item.title: GTA 5's unstoppable train has been a meme for a decade, so naturally, players wasted no time trying to stop GTA 6's train – but they were sad to find out that it wasn't all that hard to do.
item.description:
GTA 5's unstoppable train has been a meme for a decade, so naturally, players wasted no time trying to stop the one in GTA 6 – but they were sad to find out that it wasn't all that hard to do.
What better way to spend the early days of a project that Rockstar Games fans waited 13 years for than to immediately do the same thing they've already been doing? As players were dropped into the south end of Leonida, many immediately took Jason as far as they could just to find a train to stand in front of.
There is, indeed, a new train screeching over the tracks surrounding Vice City, but there's a problem – it has no aura.
Finally, the train in GTA 6 has come to stop 😭😭😭😭 https://t.co/ly0JOJ0Mb0
So sánh tàu hỏa đối đầu với các phương tiện trong GTA5 vs GTA6 vs PDR2 https://t.co/M4CwCbgokx
If you're one of the few people who hasn't picked up GTA 5 since it launched in 2013, you still may have heard about its unstoppable train. The iconic black, yellow, and white locomotive patrols Los Santos and has for years, and unlike just about every other vehicle in the game, there's nothing Michael, Franklin, or Trevor can do to stop it.
Dumb trucks, C4, planes, rows of cars – you name it. No one has ever been able to get GTA 5's train to budge. After 13 years of trying, it's become a meme on the internet to try and move the train, resulting in countless videos that have cropped up from those seeking to test its mettle (and farm a bit of engagement on social media).
Naturally, GTA 6 presented an updated take on the opportunity when players discovered its train. Unfortunately, Rockstar's commitment to realism means moving the new locomotive isn't just possible; it's actually kind of easy. Crash into it with a dump truck? Works like a charm. Park an excavator in its path? Stops it in its tracks. Raise a bridge? Completely detailed. Rockstar's new, smarter NPCs even have the brains to pull the brakes when they see a person simply standing in their way.
This is where we get into the argument that has plagued Rockstar both inside and outside of the studio for years: When is a game too realistic? Judging by GTA 6's record-breaking earnings and all-time great reviews, it seems the developers' new playground struck a nice balance between being grounded and goofy. Of course, that hasn't stopped a small section of players from being upset that Leonida plays by many of the same rules that we do in the real world.
After GTA 5's train spent more than a decade as the running champ of viral videos to come out of Los Santos, players aren't ready to let GTA 5's train go. In fact, some have began to almost deify the 2013 locomotive, creating fan edits showing the last train as the superior vehicle in the locomotive power-scaling battle.
"Yeah, this and the 'No first-person mode' are the biggest downsides for me," one X/Twitter user said.
